subject: TempoHealth request: data disposition window exception + SIG artifacts
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@tempohealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: data disposition window exception + SIG artifacts

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this — TempoHealth's compliance team ran the SIG and flagged a gap between Redwood's default data-disposition window and our retention obligations for a subset of logs tied to PHI processing. Specifically: our clinical QA workflows require preserving request/response logs for 90 days for certain endpoints; Redwood's standard customer log TTL is 30 days.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a time-bound exception to extend retention to 90 days for the TempoHealth tenant (scoped to the clinical QA route) and document that exception for audit?
- We need a set of artifacts for our SIG reviewers: a short attestation describing the exception mechanics, an excerpt of the log-retention policy, and a completed SIG spreadsheet.

I attached the completed SIG workbook (Tempo_SIG_v2_completed.xlsx) with the specific questions marked. If you need more context on which routes/endpoints are in-scope I can share technical IDs.

We're aiming to close this for our July–August audit window, so any timelines you can provide would help.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Security & Compliance, TempoHealth
samir.patel@tempohealth.com

Attachment: Tempo_SIG_v2_completed.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 320KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@tempohealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: data disposition window exception + SIG artifacts

Samir —

Appreciate the heads up and the completed SIG. Looping in Neha (security evidence) and Rishi (legal & product policy) to scope the request. Quick answers up-front: we can entertain a time-bound retention exception for a narrow set of routes, but we need:

- exact route IDs and a clear justification (regulatory anchor + list of data types)
- the requested timebox (you asked 90 days; confirm if that is strict or "up to 90 days")
- evidence artifacts required by your auditors (we can produce an attestation but some customers want a contract amendment)

Neha / Rishi — can you advise on the evidence package we typically provide for SIG/SOC2 audits, and whether we require a POA/contract addendum for an exception of this length? I can share a redwood_log_retention_excerpt.pdf that we usually send as part of SIG kits.

Next steps: Samir, if you can send the route IDs by EOD, we'll do an initial technical feasibility check and come back with the evidence checklist and a proposed timeline.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_log_retention_excerpt.pdf (application/pdf, 85KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: data disposition window exception + SIG artifacts

Evelyn / Rishi —

Summary of what we can provide quickly and what will need review:

EVIDENCE WE CAN PRODUCE (2–3 business days):
- Scoped attestation letter (one page) stating: tenant-scoped retention extension to N days, effective dates, and administrative controls for deletion.
- Excerpt from our retention policy (PDF) with version/date stamp (attached by Evelyn).
- Exportable audit logs showing retention configuration changes and data-access logs for requested routes.

REQUIRES REVIEW / POSSIBLE LEGAL ADDENDUM (up to 10 business days):
- Contract addendum / MSA amendment for a change to retention limits (recommended for >60-day exceptions).
- Evidence around legal hold capability for customer-initiated holds (we support holds but need engagement from Legal to formalize wording).

TECHNICAL CONSTRAINTS / IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- We can implement a per-tenant, per-route retention policy in the control plane; it is applied as a configuration flag and enforced by automated deletion jobs.
- For customers with dedicated GPU pools (not applicable here), we keep a separate retention path — for TempoHealth (hosted) this is a config change only.
- We will log the config change and can emit a signed attestation for the effective period.

Suggested next steps:
1) Tempo to confirm exact endpoints/route IDs + whether the 90 days is a strict requirement.
2) Redwoods to produce attestation + retention excerpt within 3 business days.
3) If Tempo requires contract language, Rishi to prepare draft addendum and indicate expected turnaround.

I'll draft the attestation once we get the route list.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@tempohealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: TempoHealth Security <security@tempohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: data disposition window exception + SIG artifacts

Evelyn / Neha —

Thanks — attaching the list of route IDs for the clinical QA endpoints (see sheet "in_scope_routes" in the SIG workbook). The 90-day requirement is contractual for those routes; we need the retention extended to 90 days, not "up to". We also need a one-page attestation that we can include in our SIG evidence bundle and a statement confirming Redwood can support customer-initiated legal holds that prevent deletion during the hold period.

I've attached the completed SIG workbook again for convenience. If you can send the attestation as a PDF and an estimate for whether Rishi will need to prepare an addendum (and an ETA), we can plan our audit submission.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Samir
Attachment: Tempo_SIG_v2_completed.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 325KB)
